The Seller shall not sub-contract the Contract in whole or part to any entity without obtaining the prior written consent of buyer. 3. The Seller shall, notwithstanding the consent and assignment/sub-contract, remain jointly and severally liable and responsible to buyer together with the assignee/ sub-contractor, for and in respect of the due performance of the Contract and the Sellers obligations there under. 3. Desirable: Diploma/Certificate in Computer Applications. Some basic Knowledge of Accounts and Book keeping. (2) Able to perform other related tasks as and when required.

Maintaining the potted plants etc. within the office premises (h) Any other work assigned by the Administrative Auth ority/Higher Authorities. Area of Work: Office of the Pr. Commissioner of Income Tax (Central), Bhopal. 6. Purchase Preference (Centre) Purchase preference to Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs): Purchase preference will be given to MSEs as defined in Public Procurement Policy for Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs) Order, 2012 dated 23.03.2012 issued by Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises and its subsequent Orders/Notifications issued by concerned Ministry. If the bidder wants to avail the Purchase preference, the bidder must be the manufacturer of the offered product in case of bid for supply of goods. Traders are excluded from the purview of Public Procurement Policy for Micro and Small Enterprises. In respect of bid for Services, the bidder must be the Service provider of the offered Service. Relevant documentary evidence in this regard shall be uploaded along with the bid in respect of the offered product or service. If L-1 is not an MSE and MSE Seller (s) has/have quoted price within L-1+ 15% of margin of purchase preference /price band defined in relevant policy, such Seller shall be given opportunity to match L-1 price and contract will be awarded for percentage of 100% of total value. 7. Certificates Bidder's offer is liable to be rejected if they don't upload any of the certificates / documents sought in the Bid document, ATC and Corrigendum if any. 8. Buyer Added Bid Specific ATC

Buyer Added text based ATC clauses Buyer based Additional terms and condition s : · Bidder Eligibility and Registration : 1. The bidder must have its registered Head office in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh, and shall submit docum entary proof along with copies of Income Tax and GST returns. 2. The bidder should have solely involve in the business of Supplying Outsourcing Manpower. 3. The bidder’s GST registration must be valid in the State of Madhya Pradesh. 4. The bidder must possess a valid license for the State of Madhya Pradesh, which shall remain valid for the entire contract period. 5. The bidder must be registered with EPF, ESIC, Income Tax, GST, and under the Contract Labour (Reg ulation & Abolition) Act, 1970, and must submit valid documentary proof. 6. The bidder must have a turnover of atleast ₹1.25 crore in the 03 last financial years. 7. The bidder must have at least two work orders, each involving the deployment of a minimum of 13 p ersonnel in a Government Office, and must provide copies of these work orders and invoices. 8. Preference shall be given last financial year bidders with satisfactory experience in providing manpo wer services in the Income Tax Department, subject to submission of supporting documents. 9. Preference may be given to agencies holding ISO 9001:2015 and ISO 45001:2018 certifications that are solely engaged in manpower supply services, subject to submission of valid certificates. · Mandatory Submission Requirements : 1. Attendance in the pre-bid meeting is mandatory, and the Pre-Bid Participation Certificate mus t be uploaded on GeM to avoid the bid rejection. 2. The bidder shall upload a duly notarized affidavit on a ₹100/- stamp paper declaring that no criminal case or inquiry is pending or contemplated against the agency or the personnel proposed to be deployed anywh ere in India. Further, bidder should also declare that they will not charge any additional amount from any of the manpower that will be deployed in this office. · Operational and HR (Human Resources) Guidelines : 1. All deployed manpower must be between 18 and 60 years of age, physically fit, mentally sound, and pr operly trained for their duties. 2. The contractor shall maintain attendance records and, in case of absence, must provide a suitable subst itute immediately to ensure no disruption of services. . 3. This Office reserves the right to reject any of the bid/quotations without quoting any reason 4. The contractor is responsible for administrative control, leave management, discipline, and the conduct of its personnel throughout the contract. 5. The contractor shall not replace or change personnel without prior written approval from the Buyer, exc ept for misconduct, resignation, or other justified unavoidable circumstances. 6. The contractor shall not engage any sub-contractor or transfer/assign the contract to any other agency or person. 7. Manpower requirements may increase or decrease during the contract period based on actual needs, a nd the contractor must comply accordingly. · Financial and Statutory Obligations : 1. The successful bidder shall pay minimum wages as notified by the Office of the Chief Labour Commissione r (Central) and immediately implement any revisions. 2. Wages must be credited directly into the personnel's bank accounts within the first week, no later than th e 7th day of the following month, and no cash payments are permitted.

3. The successful bidder shall open EPF and ESI accounts, deposit both employer and employee contribution s, and submit all challans, receipts, and account statements with monthly bills. 4. The successful bidder shall issue monthly salary slips to all personnel clearly indicating wage components and statutory deductions. 5. The contractor shall ensure timely payment of wages for at least three months at its own cos t and risk, regardless of potential delays in bill clearance. 6. The contractor is solely responsible for compliance with all labour laws and statutory obligations; the Dep artment shall not be liable for any compensation, claims, injury, disability, or death of personnel. · Contractual Terms : 1. The contract may be extended beyond the initial period subject to satisfactory performance, mutual cons ent, and approval from the competent authority in accordance with GFR provisions. 2. Any dispute arising out of or in connection with this contract shall be subject to the jurisdiction of compet ent courts at Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh. . 9. Service & Support AVAILABILITY OF OFFICE OF SERVICE PROVIDER: An office of the Service Provider must be located in the state of Consignee. DOCUMENTARY EVIDENCE TO BE SUBMITTED. 10. Service & Support Dedicated /toll Free Telephone No. for Service Support : BIDDER/OEM must have Dedicated/toll Free Telephone No. for Service Support. 11. Service & Support Escalation Matrix For Service Support : Bidder/OEM must provide Escalation Matrix of Telephone Numbers for Service Support. 12. Service & Support The Service Provider is required to have at least 40 % of the required manpower on service provider’s payroll for at least one year. Necessary documents relating to such manpower will be uploaded by the bidder for verification of the buyer. Such manpower will be part of total manpower to be provided by the Service Provider in case he gets the contract against this bid. 13. Past Project Experience Proof for Past Experience and Project Experience clause: For fulfilling the experience criteria any one of the following documents may be considered as valid proof for meeting the experience criteria:a. Contract copy along with Invoice(s) with self-certification by the bidder that service/supplies against the invoices have been executed.b. Execution certificate by client with contract value.c. Any other document in support of contract execution like Third Party Inspection release note, etc.Proof for Past Experience and Project Experience clause: For fulfilling the experience criteria any one of the following documents may be considered as valid proof for meeting the experience criteria:a. Purchase Preference (State) Purchase preference to Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs): Purchase preference will be given to MSEs from the State of Bid Inviting Authority having valid Udyam Registration and whose credentials are validated online through Udyam Registration portal as defined in Public Procurement Policy for Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs) Order, 2012 dated 23.03.2012 issued by Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises and its subsequent Orders/Notifications issued by concerned Ministry / State of Bid inviting authority. Relevant documentary evidence in this regard shall be uploaded along with the bid in respect of the offered product or service and Buyer will decide eligibility for purchase preference based on documentary evidence submitted, while evaluating the bid. If L-1 is not an MSE and MSE Seller (s) has / have quoted price within L-1+ 15 % of margin of purchase preference /price band defined in relevant policy, such MSE Seller shall be given opportunity to match L-1 price and contract will be awarded for 100 percentage of total quantity. The buyers are advised to refer the OM No. F.1/4/2021-PPD dated 18.05.2023 OM_No.1_4_2021_PPD_dated_18.05.2023 for compliance of Concurrent application of Public Procurement Policy for Micro and Small Enterprises Order, 2012 and Public Procurement (Preference to Make in India) Order, 2017. Benefits of MSE will be allowed only if seller is validated on-line in GeM profile as well as validated and approved by Buyer after evaluation of documents submitted.
